newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Double hull prevented second Venezuela oil spill.
newsitem.headline: Double hull prevented second Venezuela oil spill.

text.p: The Olympic Sponsor oil tanker which went aground on March 10 near the Venezuelan coast was holed but did not spill any oil because the vessel had a two- layer hull, a shipping source said on Tuesday.
The Sponsor was the second tanker to run aground in the Lake Maracaibo shipping channel within two weeks and officials are still not sure why.
The single-hulled Nissos Amorgos went aground in exactly the same spot as the Sponsor on February 28, spilling at least 25,000 barrels of crude into the Caribbean.

In a telephone interview with Reuters, a shipping source close to the events said the owners of the Olympic Sponsor did not want to risk refloating it before 107,000 barrels have been removed from the 477,000 barrel cargo.
"The owner doesn't want to take any risk regarding the metal. She has a hole in the hull... but there is no pollution this time because she is double-hull."
"Unless the vessel is lighter they are not going to proceed to refloat her. We are doing that and we are planning to have her ready by Thursday at 1500 hours," he added.
The 5,000 tonne Sail Peter tanker is currently alongside the Sponsor and expected to take 85,000 barrels. A second tanker, the Neptuno II, is due to offload the remaining 27,000 barrels.

If it is refloated safely, the Sponsor is then expected to anchor just outside the channel for an inspection of the hull from on board the vessel, after which the ship will sail to Guaranao, near Punto Cardon, for inspection by divers.
"They already repaired the hole, but they need an underwater survey to confirm the repairs are in good condition. That has to be done in Punta Cardon," the source said.
Meanwhile, the trans-shipment of crude oil from the Nissos Amorgos near Punta Cardon finished at 1400 local time (1800 GMT) on Tuesday, a shipping source said.
The Nissos now contains only water in two tanks and the tanker which loaded all its crude, the Wilmington, is due to sail for Italy, he said.
